title: TSMC Eyes Texas for $22.6 Billion Semiconductor Manufacturing Facility
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

TSMC is exploring another major expansion of its US semiconductor manufacturing footprint, this time in Brazos County, Texas. According to a filing with the Texas Comptroller’s office, TSMC is seeking property tax incentives for a proposed $22.6 billion investment in advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

The proposed campus would occupy more than 3,200 acres and potentially include multiple fabs producing chips at 2nm and beyond. The project could generate more than 2,000 direct jobs, with Arizona remaining a competing location.

Texas is certainly an interesting choice. The state has a long history of semiconductor manufacturing, dating back to the early days of Texas Instruments. Samsung's substantial investments in Central Texas have further strengthened the regional semiconductor ecosystem. The proximity to Texas A&M University also presents opportunities for workforce development, engineering research, and industry collaboration.

From a strategic perspective, diversifying manufacturing locations within the United States makes sense for TSMC. Geographical diversification could reduce operational risks while expanding access to engineering talent, infrastructure, and semiconductor suppliers.

Arizona, however, has the advantage of an established TSMC manufacturing ecosystem. Replicating that infrastructure in Texas would require considerable investment and coordination with equipment vendors, materials suppliers, construction companies, and local utilities.

The economics of leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing cannot be overstated. With individual fabs costing tens of billions of dollars, government incentives can significantly influence site selection. TSMC's application under the Texas Jobs, Energy, Technology and Innovation program underscores the increasingly competitive nature of semiconductor manufacturing investment.

Bottom line: The Texas proposal is not yet a firm investment commitment, but it is another indication of TSMC's ambitions in the United States. With AI driving unprecedented demand for advanced semiconductor technology, the question may ultimately be less about Texas versus Arizona and more about how quickly TSMC can bring additional leading-edge manufacturing capacity online.
